rendered.overview: A non-black Ally and Lesson deck led by [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]]. Ramp and cheap Lessons set off airbending, earthbending, firebending and waterbending, which draw cards and flip the commander. The flipped side deals 4 damage to each opponent. [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander together make a looping alternate win.

strategy: Ramp with [[Bender's Waterskin]] and [[Great Divide Guide]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Airbend, earthbend, firebend and waterbend in one turn so [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] draws and transforms.
Flip it, then each upkeep draw four, gain 4 and deal 4 to each opponent with [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].
Backup: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] loop for infinite ETBs.

keep: [[Hermitic Herbalist]] fixes colors for an early commander.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] turns every spell into an earthbend.
sendBack: Hands that cannot make white, blue and red together.
Expensive Lessons with no ramp to cast them.

tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] airbends [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], and recasting from exile for {2} makes an Ally token.
[[Uncle Iroh]] discounts Lessons, and each Lesson cast makes [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbend with an extra counter.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles the enter trigger of the Ally [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], airbending twice.

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Draws on every bend, then flips to drain.
Airbends on entry and loops with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]].
Flash body that airbends your permanents.
Cheapens Lessons and firebends when attacking.
Earthbends whenever you cast a spell.
Makes every land and Ally tap for mana.
Taps for any color on opponents' turns too.

weaknesses: Moderate: Only 2 interaction cards, 1 at instant speed, so a fast combo like [[Thassa's Oracle]] is hard to stop in time.
Moderate: The draw and flip plan needs [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], and [[Swords to Plowshares]] stalls it.
Minor: Lesson counts in the graveyard matter, and [[Rest in Peace]] shuts off [[Gran-Gran]] and [[Bumi, King of Three Trials]].

rendered.overview: This Jeskai artifact deck leans on [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and a pile of proliferate effects to grow charge and +1/+1 counters. Ramp and artifact draw build the board, [[Lux Artillery]] can burn the table once thirty counters are out, and a few listed combos give alternate finishes.

strategy: Ramp with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and talismans, then cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] each turn to proliferate, with [[Surge Conductor]] adding more as artifacts enter.
Grow counters on creatures and artifacts, double them with [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]], then finish with [[Lux Artillery]].
Backup: [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] together make infinite turns.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] with early mana to cast it.
Cheap artifact ramp leading into [[Thought Monitor]].
sendBack: Expensive proliferate pieces with no early mana to cast them.
Hands missing blue or white sources for your spells.

tips.text: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] taps to proliferate, and [[Pemmin's Aura]] untaps it for {U}, so each untap gives another proliferate.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] makes every proliferate happen twice, doubling the value of [[Contagion Engine]] activations.
[[Surge Conductor]] proliferates whenever a nontoken artifact enters, so [[Whir of Invention]] puts an artifact in play and proliferates.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it becomes tapped.
Proliferates when artifacts enter.
Doubles each proliferate you make.
Deals 10 damage with thirty counters.
Untaps Kilo for repeated proliferate.
Extra turns from charge counters.
Pairs with Zirda for infinite mana.
Finds the artifact the plan needs.

weaknesses: Critical: Nearly the whole deck is artifacts, so [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]] shuts down its engines and ramp.
Moderate: Removal on [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], such as [[Swords to Plowshares]], loses the main proliferate engine.
Minor: Only 6 interaction cards, and a fast combo can beat [[Dovin's Veto]] because it cannot stop creature-based wins.

backups: Assemble [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] together to make infinite turns and a lock.
Pair [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana to fund proliferate and activated abilities.

rendered.overview: This colorless Eldrazi and artifact deck piles up mana from rocks and utility lands, then casts big colorless spells. [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] gives those spells double cascade, and annihilator creatures like [[Artisan of Kozilek]] finish the game. [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] make infinite colorless mana as an alternate route.

strategy: Play rocks like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Thran Dynamo]] to reach the commander's cost quickly.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5, then cast mana value 7 or greater colorless spells from hand for double cascade.
Land [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] to attack with annihilator and take what opponents sacrifice.
Backup: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Thran Dynamo]] or another big rock with a cheap play to follow.
[[Eye of Ugin]] with Eldrazi to cast off it.
sendBack: Hands with only expensive spells and no rocks to cast them.

tips.text: [[Forsaken Monument]] doubles colorless mana from [[Basalt Monolith]], and untapping the Monolith loops it into infinite mana.
[[Artisan of Kozilek]] returns a creature when cast, and cast from hand it gets double cascade with [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
[[Eye of Ugin]] makes colorless Eldrazi cheaper and can fetch [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] later.

Adds three colorless mana for big casts.
Cheapens Eldrazi and finds colorless creatures.
Recurs a creature and attacks with annihilator.

Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] gets past it.
Minor: Without [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] the deck loses double cascade, though the big colorless spells still work.

backups: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana, which powers [[Blast Zone]] and [[Steel Hellkite]] as outlets.

rendered.overview: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] leads a Naya Dinosaur deck that ramps into big creatures, then attacks with haste and trample so Gishath can reveal and drop more Dinosaurs. Enrage creatures, fight effects and cost reducers fill out the plan, and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] is an alternate route to infinite tokens.

strategy: Play mana creatures and land fetchers like [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]] and [[Topiary Stomper]] to reach the big Dinosaurs.
Discount Dinosaurs with [[Kinjalli's Caller]] and [[Knight of the Stampede]], then cast them in bulk.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and use trample to reveal cards and put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Alternate win: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] together make infinite creature tokens when Dinosaurs enter.

keep: [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]] on an early turn with a second mana source.
[[Topiary Stomper]] plus a cheap Dinosaur to follow it.
sendBack: Expensive Dinosaurs with no way to ramp toward them.
Hands missing red or white for the colors this deck needs.

tips.text: [[Polyraptor]] copies itself when damaged, and [[Marauding Raptor]] deals 2 damage to each creature entering, so each copy triggers the next.
[[Rite of Passage]] adds counters when creatures survive damage, which fits [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] enrage triggers.
[[Lightning Greaves]] gives [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] shroud so it can connect safely.

keyCards.job: Combat damage puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Adds two mana for creature spells.
Makes Dinosaur spells cost less.
Discovers a spell when Dinosaurs enter.
Finds Dinosaurs and pings on each entry.
Copies itself whenever it is damaged.
Makes Beasts and casts creatures from the top.

weaknesses: Moderate: No interaction is at instant speed, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] cannot be stopped in time.
Moderate: Most wins come through combat, so [[Propaganda]] or fog effects slow the plan.
Minor: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] costs 8, so [[Swords to Plowshares]] on it costs a lot of tempo.

rendered.overview: This Red Goblin deck casts [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 and doubles its Goblin count each turn. [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Goblin Chieftain]] give haste so the swarm attacks at once, while burn clears blockers. A listed combo with [[Skirk Prospector]] makes infinite tokens.

strategy: Deploy cheap Goblins like [[Mogg War Marshal]] and [[Dragon Fodder]] so [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] has a large count to double.
Cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 and tap it each turn to multiply the Goblin army.
Give the army haste and size with [[Goblin Chieftain]] and [[Goblin Warchief]], then swing wide.
Backup: [[Goblin Warchief]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] together make infinite tokens and death triggers.
Alternate win: [[Fireball]] or [[Goblin Grenade]] fires burn at the table when blockers stall the swarm.

keep: [[Mogg War Marshal]] on an early curve feeds the commander.
[[Goblin Chieftain]] with cheap Goblins to give haste.
sendBack: Burn and pump with no Goblins to carry them.
Hands with only expensive spells and no early plays.

tips.text: [[Goblin Chieftain]] gives other Goblins haste, so tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can attack the turn they are made.
[[Pashalik Mons]] pings for each Goblin that dies, so sacrificing to [[Goblin Bombardment]] adds extra damage.

keyCards.job: Doubles the Goblin count every turn.
Gives Goblins haste and +1/+1.
Cheaper Goblins that all have haste.
Turns spare Goblins into red mana.
Makes two bodies for Krenko to count.
Finds the Goblin the deck needs.
Turns extra Goblins into damage.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck has artifact removal but nothing that answers an enchantment such as [[Propaganda]] or [[Ghostly Prison]].
Moderate: Repeated removal on [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] slows token growth, such as [[Swords to Plowshares]].
Moderate: Mostly combat wins, so a sweeper like [[Wrath of God]] wipes out the whole Goblin board.

plans.primary: Build a wide Goblin army with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and token makers, then win by attacking with hasty Goblins backed by pump and burn.
backups: Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite commander casts, hasty tokens, death triggers and enter-the-battlefield triggers.
Finish with direct damage from [[Fireball]], [[Goblin Grenade]] and [[Guttersnipe]] when combat is blocked.

rendered.overview: This Jeskai partner deck runs [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] over a pile of God creatures, proliferate effects and counter payoffs. Experience counters grow a creature each end step, [[All Will Be One]] turns counters into damage, and extra combats finish the job.

strategy: Ramp with rocks, then cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] around turn 4.
Attack with Gods and let them die to build experience counters, so each end step [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] adds more +1/+1 counters.
Proliferate with [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Flux Channeler]] to raise counters, and [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds extra.
Cash counters in with [[All Will Be One]] for damage, and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] draws cards per experience counter.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] or [[World at War]] adds combat phases for a big counter-laden attacker.

keep: [[Thought Vessel]] with a way to reach four mana early.
[[Contentious Plan]] alongside a God or counter piece.
sendBack: Hands missing white or blue sources for the Gods.
Expensive payoffs with no ramp to cast them.

tips.text: [[Inexorable Tide]] proliferates on every spell, and each counter added triggers [[All Will Be One]] for damage.
[[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter whenever you get experience from [[Kratos, Stoic Father]].

keyCards.job: Gains experience, grows a creature each end step.
Draws per experience and pings opponents.
Turns each counter placed into damage.
Proliferates on every spell cast.
Adds an extra counter whenever counters are placed.
Doubles each proliferate.
Adds extra combat phases for a backup win.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many key enchantments like [[All Will Be One]] and [[Inexorable Tide]] fall to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Disenchant]], and the deck has little answer to them.
Moderate: Experience counters and growth rely on [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], so removal such as [[Swords to Plowshares]] on it slows the plan.
Moderate: Combat is the main route, so a board wipe or fog like [[Settle the Wreckage]] stalls the plan.

backups: Use extra combat phases from [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] to turn a large attacker into lethal damage.
Ping opponents with [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]], [[All Will Be One]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] as counters and creatures pile up.

rendered.overview: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] leads a Mono-blue Wizard deck full of counterspells, cantrips and cheap flash creatures. rendered.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninjutsu deck. Cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Tormented Soul]] connect, then ninjutsu Ninjas swap in for card advantage and drain. Counterspells and cheap removal protect the attack, and extra-turn spells give more combat steps.

strategy: Cast cheap unblockable creatures such as [[Slither Blade]] and [[Triton Shorestalker]] to get unblocked attackers.
Activate ninjutsu with [[Mistblade Shinobi]] or [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]], returning the unblocked attacker to hand.
Put [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] in from the command zone around turn 3 so each Ninja hit drains life.
Hold counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Negate]] up to protect the attackers.
Backup: chain extra turns with [[Time Warp]] and [[Temporal Trespass]] for more attacks.

keep: [[Slither Blade]] plus a cheap ninjutsu Ninja starts the engine.
Blue and black sources with [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] in hand.
sendBack: Only expensive Ninjas and no unblockable creature to enable them.
Counterspells alone, with no creature to start attacking.

tips.text: [[Silver-Fur Master]] cuts ninjutsu costs by 1 and gives other Ninjas +1/+1, so [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] hits harder.
[[Reanimate]] on a creature that [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] steals from a graveyard adds more bodies for the attack.
